question: Orally administered proton pump inhibitor drugs:

options.opa: Neutralize hydrochloric acid from gastric secretion.

analysis: Orally administered proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are designed to inhibit the hydrogen-potassium ATPase enzyme system (proton pump) of the gastric parietal cells, thereby reducing gastric acid secretion. They do not neutralize hydrochloric acid, block histaminergic or gastrin receptors. PPIs are acid-labile and require an enteric coating to prevent degradation in the stomach, ensuring they reach the intestine where they can be absorbed effectively.
